result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain the gamut limit, push back on the printer and recommend a Pantone spot color, so they are close. A is more honest about the result: it says outright that print won't reproduce the glow of a backlit screen. Its CMYK fallback, a printed test sheet on the actual paper, also suits a bakery owner better than B's Illustrator soft-proofing steps. B gains points for its ready-made script to give the printer and its accent-use tip, but it implies a spot ink can fully capture the screen orange and leans on more technical work. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain the screen-versus-ink limit well, separate it from the parts the bakery can fix, and recommend a Pantone spot color, a coated stock and a physical proof. B is clearer that an exact match isn't possible ('won't reproduce the glow of a backlit screen'; hex-to-Pantone matches are only approximate). B's printed test sheet of several orange versions is also easier for a bakery owner to act on than A's DIY soft-proofing in Illustrator. Both use some jargon (ICC profiles, GRACoL/FOGRA), but A's step 2 asks the owner to do technical work, while B frames most technical points as questions to ask the printer.
